title: Applied Intuition Fields Offers at $30 Billion Valuation
source_used: KuCoin news flash (relaying IT Home, which relays The Information) plus The Information public teaser; The Information is paywalled
key_facts: The Information reported on 13 Oct 2026 that autonomous-driving software start-up Applied Intuition has received multiple investment offers at a valuation of at least $30 billion, double its valuation in June.
Applied Intuition was co-founded by Qasar Younis, a former Y Combinator chief operating officer, and Peter Ludwig, a former Google product manager.
It focuses on autonomous-driving software rather than building vehicles.
It previously raised $1.2 billion from investors including Andreessen Horowitz and General Catalyst.
Major clients include Isuzu and Volkswagen.

The Information's introduction says a growing number of start-ups making AI-powered apps, agents or software are fetching valuations of $20 billion or higher, after three years in which AI labs such as OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI drew most investor attention.
quote_evidence: IT Home, October 13 news: According to The Information today, autonomous driving startup Applied Intuition has received multiple investment offers, with a valuation of at least $30 billion (IT Home note: approximately RMB 201.175 billion at current exchange rates), doubling its valuation from June.
Applied Intuition previously raised $1.2 billion from institutions such as Andreessen Horowitz and General Catalyst, with major clients including Isuzu and Volkswagen.

notes: The Information is paywalled; read the KuCoin/IT Home relay and the public teaser. A GuruFocus page also carries the story but mixes in unrelated C3.ai data and an annual-recurring-revenue figure dated "end of 2024", so it was not used. These are offers, not a closed round.
